name: Fullerton & Botsford

partners.name: Botsford
partners.basis: The firm's own style prints this partner's surname (Fullerton & Botsford); no notice prints him apart from the house. Linked to the town card botsford_j_k at inferred (T-2245): The pork notice is signed 'FULLERTON & BOTSFORD, corner of Dearborn and Lake-sts.' (chicago_democrat_1834_06_04#c024, copy dated April 22, 1834), and the corner of Dearborn and Lake is the frontage J. K. Botsford's own grocery and tin shop advertises from in the same weeks (identity.json, refused_anchor_changes on business_j_k_botsford, T-0324). identity.json's proprietor merges on that house rule that nothing in the corpus names a second Botsford. One Botsford, one corner: the partner is J. K. Botsford. Dated by the printing window, which bounds the reading and does not date the partnership.

locations.basis: The paper names a street and no house on it.
locations.limit_reason: The paper names Dearborn Street and nothing narrower; a corner of 'Dearborn' and 'Lake-sts. corner of Dearborn and Lake-st', and the plat resolves both sides to ['dearborn', 'lake'].

dates.basis: No opening is announced. The first printing, 1834-06-04, is the bound: the house was trading by then and the record does not say when it began.

proprietor_community.basis: The 1 keeper(s) this record names and the resident layer holds a card for all read yankee: Botsford (yankee). A house is not its keeper, so the reading is an inference about the house and is capped there.

replaceable_by: A directory, a deed or a later reading that names this house's premises, its staff or its dates more exactly than the newspapers do.
